# Generated by `caf gen chart` from this project's cafaye.yml.

# courier

The Helm chart courier is deployed from. The templates are the
contract; `values.yaml` is the deployment-time half — the file the
values commit edits.

## The loop

The chart is deployed by ArgoCD, pull-only. The substrate's own
Application manifest
(`kit/templates/substrate/manifests/applications/courier.yaml`) names
`oci://ghcr.io/cafaye/charts` chart `courier` targetRevision `0.1.0`,
and Argo pulls this chart from the fleet's private OCI registry. The
only thing that can change the cluster is a commit. Push a values
commit, Argo syncs, the box agrees with git. A hand edit self-heals;
rollback is `git revert`.

**This chart ships no `templates/application.yaml`.** The generator
emits one, but the substrate already owns courier's Application —
two Applications named `courier` in `argocd` fight each other. The
generated one was removed deliberately; see the CHANGELOG.

## Shipping the chart

The chart ships from the fleet's private OCI registry, because the
substrate is closed source and a pull-based system needs somewhere to
pull from:

    helm package chart
    helm push chart-0.1.0.tgz oci://ghcr.io/cafaye/charts/courier

The box pulls it with the read-only secret `values.yaml` names
(`imagePullSecrets`), created on the box once, out of band. The chart
names the secret and never contains a credential.

## Secrets

The service's environment arrives by reference: the Deployment reads
the secret `values.yaml` names (`secretName`) with `envFrom`. Create
it on the box:

    kubectl create secret generic courier-secrets --from-literal=...

Rotate a value by replacing the secret and restarting the pods — not
by editing a generated file.

## Readiness

The probe is `/readyz`. That is the fleet's contract: every cafaye
service serves it, and the rollout waits on it. It is baked into the
template rather than left as a value, because a readiness path that
can be edited is a readiness path that can be pointed at `/up` — the
defect the kamal template had, which produced deploys that could
never go green.
